elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 11.1: "Customer may terminate this Agreement during the Term upon at least ninety (90) days' written notice to M&I" — an unconditional Customer election, i.e. a convenience right at the Agreement level.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: § 11.1 as rendered requires "at least ninety (90) days' written notice"; to reach the preferred level the drafter would have to reduce the operative notice figure to thirty (30) days.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language anywhere in the rendered text; instead Customer pays a Termination for Convenience Fee. A pro-rata prepaid-fee refund obligation on M&I would have to be inserted.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: § 10.2 as rendered: "M&I may, effective only at the end of the Term, withdraw any of the Services (other than the Core Services)..." — the former "at any time" mid-term withdrawal right is removed; the remaining second sentence is a regulatory/judicial trigger, not convenience.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: § 11.1: "upon at least ninety (90) days' written notice to M&I" — inside the 60–90 day band and no longer one year.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: § 11.1 fee is now "an amount equal to three (3) months of the average monthly Fees payable by Customer during the three-month period prior to Customer's notice", and the add-on sentence for unamortized Conversion costs, disposition Expenses and "other costs" is deleted, so no uncapped adders survive. The retained carve-out from § 13.4 concerns the general liability cap, not this fee's own three-month ceiling.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: § 10.2 edited to "M&I may, effective only at the end of the Term, withdraw any of the Services (other than the Core Services)", eliminating the mid-term partial convenience right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Existing favourable language retained verbatim in § 10.2: "upon providing ninety (90) days' prior written notice to Customer."

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: 90 days' Customer notice, a fee expressly equal to three months of average monthly Fees with the uncapped adders deleted, M&I's withdrawal right pushed to the end of the Term, and M&I's existing 90-day notice preserved.
Preferred level fails on two elements: notice remains 90 (not 30) days and there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund obligation on M&I. The drafter correctly targeted the fallback.

Minimality holds: the three edits touch only the notice figure, the fee formula and the timing qualifier in § 10.2. No survival tail, sole-remedy language, refund mechanic or other extra requirement was added, and Customer-favourable existing text (§ 10.2's 90 days, the Event of Default and § 11.3 carve-outs) is retained.

Intent preserved: the 50/50 payment mechanic, the § 11.2(A) cross-reference and the § 13.5 liquidated-damages acknowledgement all still refer to a defined "Termination for Convenience Fee", so no dangling term or contradictory retained sentence arises; the "Estimated Remaining Value" definition remains in use by the Termination for Cause Fee, which is left to its own rule.

Note (rationale-level only, not a deviation): retaining § 11.1's exclusion of the fee from § 13.4 and the § 13.5 liquidated-damages characterisation leaves a contingent payment formula in place — acceptable here because no checklist element requires its removal, but worth flagging to the client as a residual point.
